title: Affine perfect support extension
statement: Let X be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let T be a closed subset of X whose complement is quasi-compact, and let U be a quasi-compact open of X. For every perfect object F of D(\mathcal O_U) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex] whose cohomology sheaves vanish on U\setminus(T\cap U), there exists a perfect object E of D(\mathcal O_X) whose cohomology sheaves vanish on X\setminus T and such that E|_U is isomorphic to F\oplus F[1].

proof.text: Apply exists_perfect_restrict_iso_directSum_shift to obtain a perfect E0 whose restriction is F plus F[1]. Obtain finitely many powered generators cutting out T whose restrictions act by zero on F.

Construct a sequence of cones using Mathlib distinguished_cocone_triangle: extend g by zero to a sequence indexed by the natural numbers, recursively choose each cone, and restrict the resulting sequence to Fin(s+1). Its initial term is E0 and every adjacent triple is a distinguished scalar cone triangle.

Apply affine_support_iterated_cones to this actual cone chain. The last term A is perfect, vanishes at every point in a principal open D(g_i), and restricts to the binomial biproduct. The powered-generator cover identifies this support with T.

Choose the projector supplied by exists_binomial_projector_cone_restrict. Perfectness gives quasi-coherent cohomology for A. Apply exists_perfect_map_lift_of_isAffine with target A to get A-prime, beta and gamma, the compatible restriction isomorphism, and support of A-prime on T.

The supported quasi-coherent property is triangulated, so take a supported distinguished cone of gamma. Perfect two-out-of-three proves its perfectness. The projector-cone calculation identifies its restriction with F plus F[1]. This cone is the required E.
